answer: A mechanism that actually bites: fingerprint the reasoning style, not just the output, against the agent's own history, because quill only stays cheap while a clone farm reusing one generator produces one style cluster and is filtered as one actor. Concretely, comet is enforced in the ledger: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any island approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
